title: HDFC Bank sends two names to RBI for MD, CEO post- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: The names were provided in order of preference, along with the proposed remuneration for a three-year term subject to RBI approval, the bank said in an exchange filing    September 12, 2026 / 20:31 IST             HDFC Bank's Board of Directors on Saturday approved the appointment process for the bank's Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, including "submitting the names of two candidates in order of preference and the remuneration proposed to be paid to them, for a period of three years, subject to approval of RBI." In an exchange filing, the bank said the proposal was approved based on the recommendations of the Governance, Nomination and Remuneration Committee and pursuant to the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025. The proposal will be submitted to the Reserve Bank of India for approval. The board also approved the "re-appointment of V Srinivasa Rangan as a Whole-time Director (designated as Executive Director) of the Bank along with remuneration payable to him with effect from November 23, 2026 till November 22, 2027." It further approved the "appointment of Jimmy Tata as a Whole-time Director (designated as Executive Director) of the Bank along with remuneration payable to him, for a period of 3 (three) years with effect from the date of approval of RBI or such other date/ period specified by RBI." The leadership changes come as incumbent MD & CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan is set to retire in October. Rangan, 66, is currently an Executive Director of HDFC Bank, overseeing human resources, corporate legal, group oversight and secretarial functions, investment banking, information security, ethics, and fraud and vigilance. He was earlier Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer of HDFC Ltd before its amalgamation with HDFC Bank in July 2023. Tata has more than 35 years of experience in the banking and financial services sector and has been associated with HDFC Bank since 1994. He is currently the bank's Chief Credit Officer and had earlier served as its Chief Risk Officer. The leadership proposals remain subject to regulatory approvals, with the bank expected to seek shareholder approval where required.
